stories.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 12
stories.summary: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's ranks are here to help.
stories.body:
The Week 12 flex and superflex rankings begin with two of fantasy's top scorers -- Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs and Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba -- among the top three. Gibbs will get the party started on Thursday, but remember, Week 12 starts quite early this week, with the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. Suffice to say, with Gibbs and three of the six QBs averaging at least 20 points per game playing Thursday, plenty of fantasy points will be scored before we even get to the weekend.

Fantasy managers may notice a different hierarchy of quarterbacks near the top, as Buffalo Bills star Josh Allen has slipped a bit in the scoring column recently. Houston Texans starter C.J. Stroud, however, is streaking, and comes in at an aggressive No. 2 at QB this week, thanks in part to a friendly matchup against a struggling Baltimore Ravens defense that has permitted 30 or more traditional points in four of five games. Deshaun Watson and Fernando Mendoza, who square off on Sunday night, are other passers ranked among our top 30 superflex options this week.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from the games on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

stories.headline: Williams F1 boss admits 'shocking year' and explains budget cap breach
stories.summary: Williams team principal James Vowles has labelled 2026 as an "absolutely shocking year" for his team, but believes the recent pain was necessary to lay groundwork for long-term progress.
stories.body:
Williams team principal James Vowles has labelled 2026 as an "absolutely shocking year" for his team, but believes the recent pain was necessary to lay groundwork for long-term progress.

Since joining Williams in 2023, Vowles has targeted this year's regulation change as an opportunity to move one of the sport's most famous teams back up the grid.

However, delays to the car's build ahead of the season and a package that ultimately proved overweight and down on performance at the start of the year has seen the team slip from fifth in the constructors' championship in 2025 to ninth this year.

To make matters worse, last week the FIA announced Williams had overspent under last year's budget cap and would face a 1.5% reduction in its wind tunnel and CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) development time next year as a penalty.

Vowles explained that the £627,000 overspend was a result of necessary restructuring for the company's future, but admitted the challenges the team has faced in 2026 meant it had been the hardest of his four years leading the team.

"It's been the toughest year, yes, there's no doubt about it," he said. "I mean, we've been very pretty much open and honest; it's been an absolutely shocking year.

"We have two world-class drivers [Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon], and we haven't delivered a car that is even close to respecting their ability. But I also think we have to go through a year like this because last year, what we could prove is in a consistent set of regulations, we can do a reasonable job and produce a reasonable car.

"The true test of a team is can you do that back-to-back, and can you do that through regulation change? And we've proven not, but it's allowed us to make quite a few changes underneath the hood as a result of it. So, tough year, but one I think we had to go through."

- Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli leads George Russell in first practice

- Qatar GP organisers keen to show world 'real situation' amid safety concerns

- George Russell breaks silence on Max Verstappen criticism: 'Amusing'

Vowles stressed that Williams believed it was within the cost cap last year and only discovered it had overspent when the FIA completed its investigation a few weeks ago.

"The background to it is that the company structure of Williams was largely unchanged from 1977 and wasn't really fit for purpose in a modern world," he explained. "We went into it with every intention of being open and transparent with the FIA, which is what we held all the way throughout, but believed those costs, because it's company restructuring, not to be a cost cap expense.

"It was the company restructuring that put us over, and as you saw, put us over by £600,000 in that circumstance. The FIA themselves have noted, and we haven't had any financial benefit from it, no sporting benefit as a result of it. And you can see that the penalty is pretty much adjusted to be in line with that as well at the same time.

"But it was our interpretation that those costs are out of cap. The FIA's interpretation of it is that they are in cap. And obviously, we went with the FIA's interpretation after much discussion."

Vowles said the sporting penalty for exceeding the cost cap, which was set at a 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD time, would not have a major impact on the team going forward and amounted to "small beans in the grand scheme of things."

stories.headline: The Connor McDavid Scoring Tracker: Can the Oilers' superstar break 200 points?
stories.summary: Follow along game by game as No. 97 looks to break a benchmark that only No. 99 has done in NHL history.
stories.body:
There have been only four occasions in NHL history when a player scored 200 or more points in a single season, and only one player has accomplished the feat: Wayne Gretzky.

The Great One scored 215 points in 1985-86, 212 in '81-82, 208 in '84-85 and 205 in '83-84. Mario Lemieux came closest to Gretzky, finishing the '88-89 season with 199.

Connor McDavid plays for the same Edmonton Oilers franchise that Gretzky did when he posted those totals, and his personal best total is 153, set in 2022-23.

There are cases for and against McDavid breaking the 200-point barrier this season, as his pace fluctuates on a game-by-game basis.

stories.headline: Wemby tops Luka in MVP duel, Spurs teach Lakers valuable playoff lesson
stories.summary: Victor Wembanyama's Spurs got the better of Luka Doncic's Lakers in an NBA Cup game with playoff-like intensity on Friday night.
stories.body:
The NBA's two main characters met for the first time this season Friday in a fierce contest that was still in doubt until the final buzzer sounded.

Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs got the better of Luka Doncic's Los Angeles Lakers, but only after erasing a 20-point deficit to grind out a 99-96 victory at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. Round 1 between the two MVP favorites doubled as a do-or-die NBA Cup contest. By winning, the Spurs advanced to the in-season tournament's quarterfinals, eliminated the Lakers and reclaimed the Western Conference's No. 1 seed in one fell swoop.

While Wembanyama and Doncic served as compelling foils, this highly anticipated showdown between European superstars was ultimately decided by their respective supporting casts. San Antonio prevailed in a game with playoff-like intensity because Wembanyama enjoyed just a little more help.

"I liked how my guys reacted," Wembanyama said. "It just showed character."

Wembanyama, enormous in size and stoic in demeanor, finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, two blocks and four steals. The 7-foot-4 French center delivered his strongest MVP argument midway through the fourth quarter, driving past center Walker Kessler for a two-hand reverse dunk on one end before swatting guard Collin Sexton's shot on the Lakers' next possession.

It's hard to imagine a player more valuable than Wembanyama because -- like the movie -- he has a knack for being "Everything Everywhere All at Once."

But then there's the fiery Doncic, who scored 13 of his game-high 31 points during one of his signature tone-setting first quarter bursts. The Slovenian guard is the NBA's scoring leader (36.6 ppg), and he averages 13.8 points per first quarter -- nearly four more than anyone else in the league. True to form, he had the Spurs back on their heels early.

Though Doncic struggled to shoot from outside, his elite in-between game and controlled pace were crucial ingredients to unlocking San Antonio's third-ranked defense. Doncic didn't need to challenge Wembanyama at the rim because he can create a quality floater, runner or mid-range jumper from any distance. That ability to take advantage of empty space helped give the Lakers a healthy 16-point halftime edge.

Despite scoring just 14 points in the first quarter and missing their first 10 3-point attempts, the Spurs kept their composure and blitzed the Lakers in the third quarter. San Antonio's quickness overwhelmed Los Angeles' ballhandlers and forced a string of turnovers, and guard Stephon Castle built momentum that carried into the final period.

Castle, a physical defender who possesses the size, quickness and motor to wear on Doncic, outplayed the Lakers' star in the fourth quarter, finishing with 26 points and nine assists. Midway through the period, the 2024 lottery pick hit back-to-back three-pointers to give San Antonio an eight-point lead. And in the game's final minute, he came to Wembanyama's aid with a heroic dagger.

Wembanyama went to the line with 57 seconds left and made his first attempt to give San Antonio a 93-90 lead. He proceeded to miss his second attempt, however, and the ball was tipped to the left side of the court during the battle for the rebound.

Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox tracked down the offensive rebound by beating Lakers forward Jake LaRavia and Kessler to the loose ball. Fox then passed to Castle, who drilled his fourth 3-pointer of the night.

"[Castle] is built for the moment, he wants the moment, and he attacks the moment," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

Castle's reload 3-pointer was backbreaking punishment for the Lakers' inattentiveness on the glass, the exact type of sequence that can tilt high-stakes games in May and June. In this one, Castle's shot helped San Antonio survive a pair of regrettable turnovers in the closing seconds.

"To beat these teams, you can't have those momentary mental lapses," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "We had a few of those. ... That's the barometer in the West right now. This was a great test for us, and we'll get better from it."

The Spurs' resolve also served as a reminder that Wembanyama, Castle, Fox and most of the Spurs' rotation players advanced to the Finals together last season, while the Lakers furnished Doncic and guard Austin Reaves with a new-look supporting cast during an offseason overhaul. Shared experience counts in close games.

Even so, the Lakers looked like they belonged against the reigning Western Conference champions. If Doncic had shot better than 1-of-13 from deep or if Reaves had been less sloppy in his first action after missing five games with a heel injury, they easily could have stolen the road win and advanced to the NBA Cup quarterfinals. Instead, Doncic capped the frustrating night by getting into a courtside confrontation with a fan on his way off the court.

Doncic's sour exit was nothing more than meaningless theatrics in the moment, but it will add to the intrigue when the Lakers (15-4) and Spurs (16-4) meet down the road. The "Wemby vs. Luka" MVP debate is bound to rage all season, and it could reach a fever pitch by April if these two decorated franchises keep tracking towards their playoff matchup since 2013.

"As a team, I wasn't sure what [the Lakers] were built of, just from the start of the season," said Wembanyama, whose Spurs will play at the Dallas Mavericks on Friday, Dec. 4, in the next NBA Cup game. "But it's real. It's for real. They're good."

The Spurs are real and good, too, and not just because of their superstar headliner's two-way dominance. They struck first blood against the Lakers because the smallest guy on the court made a hustle play that set up the biggest shot of the night.

stories.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is still considering his options despite his contract extension, while Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister is in Real Madrid's sights. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

stories.headline: Source: Cubs agree to terms with Japanese pitcher Hiromi Itoh
stories.summary: The Cubs continued a busy month by agreeing to terms with Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh on Friday night, a source told ESPN on Friday, confirming a report by FanSided.
stories.body:
The Chicago Cubs continued a busy month by agreeing to terms with Japanese right-hander Hiromi Itoh on Friday night, a source confirmed to ESPN, adding him alongside countryman Teruaki Sato and plugging Itoh into a needy rotation.

Itoh, 29, joins the Cubs four days after they signed left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract and three days after adding Sato, who is expected to play right field, on a six-year, $120 million deal. Both those agreements became official Friday.

Terms of Itoh's deal have not been disclosed.

During his six seasons with Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball, Itoh led the league in innings pitched (1,000⅔) and strikeouts (902), made at least 23 starts each season and won the Sawamura Award -- NPB's version of the Cy Young Award -- in 2025.

This past season, the right-hander was 10-10 with a 3.18 ERA and 159 strikeouts over 172⅔ innings while walking just 4.7% of batters faced.

Itoh was a first-round pick by Hokkaido in the 2020 NPB draft, and he has had an ERA above 3.00 in just two of his six seasons. He led the Pacific League with 14 wins in 2024 and was dominant in 2025 with a league-best 196⅔ innings and 195 strikeouts while finishing second among qualified pitchers in walk rate at 3.6%.

Some scouts have questioned his overall impact in MLB because his fastball velocity is below average, sitting 90-94 mph, and he doesn't have a plus secondary pitch to rack up strikeouts, relying most on a good slider and splitter from his six-pitch mix. What is not in doubt is his durability and control.

Itoh contributed to Japan's gold medal run at the 2021 Olympics, pitching five scoreless innings in three games, and he also pitched for his country in the 2026 World Baseball Classic.

The Cubs went into the offseason desperately needing rotation help, with Shota Imanaga, Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes all becoming free agents, and Ben Brown and Cade Horton coming off surgery. Rogers and Itoh join Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera and Braxton Garrett.

With Itoh, Sato and Kaima Taira (Toronto Blue Jays) all signing, the three big NPB stars have come off the board before the anticipated Dec. 1 lockout. Japanese players have a 45-day posting window, but the CBA's expiration date of Dec. 1 truncated it by about a third.

FanSided was first to report Itoh's agreement with the Cubs.

ESPN's Kiley McDaniel contributed to this report.

stories.headline: José Mourinho hails Jude Bellingham but refuses Zinedine Zidane comparison
stories.summary: José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
stories.body:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.

Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.

The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.

"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.

"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."

Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.

Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.

"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."

- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or

- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'

The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.

Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.

"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

stories.headline: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
stories.summary: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
stories.body:
It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch.

"Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season, while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale.

Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century.

"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%.

"The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform."

Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate.

Here are the key findings.

Football leads a multisport lineup
Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports.

Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers."

The generation gap
The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams.

18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups.

35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each.

55+: "Friday Night Lights" took the lead at 17%, narrowly ahead of "A League of Their Own" at 16%. "Ted Lasso" rounded out the top three at 13%. The drop-off was sharper for teen dramas such as "All American" and "One Tree Hill," which drew 5% and 3%, respectively.

Commonalities and contrasts between sports fans and nonfans
Sports fans and nonfans found some common ground, even if they weren't watching the same shows. "Friday Night Lights" led among sports fans at 23%, followed by "Ted Lasso" at 19% and "Cobra Kai" and "A League of Their Own" at 16% each.

Among nonfans, "Cobra Kai" moved into first at 8%, with "Ted Lasso" and "A League of Their Own" tied at 7%. Coach Eric Taylor (played by Kyle Chandler) had a tougher time with that crowd, as "Friday Night Lights" drew 5%.

The biggest divide, though, was in those who selected "don't know/no opinion": 69% of nonfans compared with 28% of sports fans. The crossover appeal is there, but viewers with less interest in sports need more motivation to tune in.

The men's and women's lineups look a little different
"Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" finished first and second among both men and women, but the order differs after that. Among men, "Cobra Kai" took third at 15%, followed by "A League of Their Own" at 11%.

Women flipped those two, with "A League of Their Own" drawing 14% and "Cobra Kai" at 11%. "Make It or Break It" and "Heated Rivalry" also drew higher percentages among women than men, both at 6% to 4%.

New shows are earning their stripes
Some newer series are already finding a place alongside the familiar favorites. "Chad Powers" drew 6% overall, followed by "Heated Rivalry" at 5% and "Running Point" and "Off Campus" at 4% each.

For avid sports fans, "Chad Powers" reached 13%, matching "The Game" in that group. "Heated Rivalry," meanwhile, had its strongest showing among adults ages 18-34 at 10%. The established shows have a head start, but the newcomers are getting some playing time.

Editor's Note: These results are derived from a Seton Hall Sports Poll conducted Oct. 8 to Oct. 13, 2026, among 1,632 adults. The Poll, which is sponsored by The Sharkey Institute within Seton Hall University's Stillman School of Business, features a national representative sample from YouGov Plc., weighted on U.S. Census Bureau figures for age, gender, ethnicity, education, income and geography with a margin of error of +/- 3.0 percent.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."

stories.headline: Lionel Messi, Inter Miami's failure to retain MLS Cup due to lack of identity
stories.summary: Inter Miami's bid to retain MLS Cup ended on Round 1 of the playoffs after a season of multiple coaching changes and an over-reliance on Lionel Messi.
stories.body:
Inter Miami CF players stood in shock when the final whistle echoed throughout Scott's Miracle-Gro Field in Ohio to signal the end of the MLS playoff Round 1 series. Lionel Messi rushed to the locker room as Columbus Crew players celebrated the almost unbelievable triumph.

The reigning Major League Soccer Cup champions have been eliminated with a shocking stoppage-time winner from Santiago Rodríguez. Columbus Crew swept the best-of-three series with 3-0 and 1-0 victories, bringing Inter Miami's 2026 season to a crashing halt.

Players knew the stakes were high when heading into the second game of the series on Friday. Forward Luis Suárez admitted a loss would render the team's season a disappointment.

"It's clear that at a club like this, we have an obligation to win, getting eliminated on Friday would be a disappointment, and that's how we should see it," Suárez said on Wednesday before the match.

Head coach Cristian "Kily" González agreed. But like so many times this season, the Herons failed to live up to the sky-high expectations set by having a star-studded roster.

"Ultimately, a single mistake on the final play is what knocked us out. I'm leaving feeling very sad and disappointed, we all are," González said in the postmatch news conference.

"Obviously, after this defeat, which, in my view, was completely unfair in the last minute, I feel the team rose to the occasion and deserved to win throughout the entire match. We created the clearest scoring opportunities. But that's football for you. Naturally, we are feeling a profound sense of sadness and disappointment."

The weight of disappointment could be felt through the TV screen as the curtain came down on 2026 for Inter Miami's players, but what more could be expected from a group that has experienced three coaching changes in the span of seven months?

Inter Miami's three coaches in one season
It's difficult to remember that Inter Miami kicked off the season in February with Javier Mascherano at the helm.

Mascherano returned for a second season to continue building his trophy-winning legacy with the club by tackling the Concacaf Champions Cup. But two draws against Nashville SC in the Round of 16 series left Inter Miami out of the international competition on the first try.

The two-legged tie caught the Herons in a moment of adjustment, especially as the club entered a new era without key veterans Jordi Alba and Sergio Busquets. Mascherano attempted to form new partnerships on the field throughout the start of the season, interchanging players in the backline while figuring out how to modify the attack to suit the new signings.

The first game against Nashville saw Micael paired with Maximiliano Falcón and Sergio Reguilón as the left back, while the second leg a week later featured Gonzalo Luján as a new center back with Noah Allen on the left.

Mascherano also benched Suárez at the start of the season to play Germán Berterame as a center forward, an almost inconceivable thought now under González. The team's early lack of consistency in starting lineups should have been a warning of what was to come.

Then, in a shocking turn of events, Mascherano resigned as head coach in April and forced Inter Miami into the Guillermo Hoyos portion of the campaign.

Hoyos, who served as the team's sporting director before transitioning into interim manager, injected a different energy into the team. Suárez immediately returned to the starting lineup, becoming an indisputable part of the attack, while Berterame shifted to the wings. Ian Fray also replaced Facundo Mura as right back under new leadership.

Momentum carried the club to a 6W-1L-1D record, securing 19 out of 24 available points with the team scoring 26 goals in eight matches. But ugly realities began to creep back up as Hoyos was forced to play musical chairs with the starting lineup due to injuries and new signings.

A five-game winless streak eventually saw Hoyos replaced by González, ushering the team into its third chapter of the season, but he quickly fell into a similar pattern of rotation.

The current coach made three crucial changes to the starting lineup between the first game of the best-of-three series and the second leg, introducing Riquelme Fillipi, Matías Galarza and Fricio Caicedo. González inexplicably benched Suárez to use Fillipi, who didn't play in the first game of the playoffs.

Inter Miami's Messi-dependence
The constant changes in leadership and lineup kept Inter Miami from developing a true identity on the field, becoming increasingly dependent on Messi's magic to save the game.

Often, it worked.

Messi concluded the regular season with 26 goals and 17 assists to win the 2026 Golden Boot and carry Inter Miami to second on the Eastern Conference table. But when Messi couldn't find the back of the net, the team suffered.

In the 17 matches this season across all competitions that Messi played but did not score, Inter Miami was able to win just three (3W-6L-8D record overall).

It happened in this series against Columbus.

The Crew muted Messi in the first game of the series, limiting the Miami captain to just two shots on goal. And the team's three-on-one defending on the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner continued to work in the second leg.

Messi recorded two shots throughout the 90 minutes and zero on target, while teammates appeared to struggle when unable to find their star player in a position to receive the ball.

"We rely heavily on Leo, and that area is one of the most heavily guarded parts of the opponent's half. The opposition makes a concerted effort to cover the spaces where Leo is constantly moving," González said after the match. "Naturally, we need to look for more options elsewhere so that Leo can get involved in the play at the perfect moment."

Now, Inter Miami faces a daunting offseason with so many unanswered questions to address. The club has multiple tournaments to prepare for in 2027, and another shot at the coveted Concacaf Champions Cup. The team qualified for the upcoming competition by concluding the MLS regular season in third place of the Supporters' Shield standings.

It continues to be the team's ultimate goal and the only trophy Messi has yet to win with Inter Miami. But time is running out.

The front office will soon make roster decisions, resolving loan spells and expired contracts. Though Suárez's contract with the club ended following Friday's final whistle, he confirmed ongoing talks with the club to find a solution for the upcoming season.

The 2027 MLS spring season and Concacaf Champions Cup start in February, giving Miami time to mourn the disappointment of yet another first-round playoff exit before needing to come back stronger.

Baltimore Ravens +7 (+260 moneyline) at Houston Texans

Baltimore can win this contest Sunday with running back Derrick Henry. Houston is allowing just 96.1 rushing yards per game but has given up 12 rushing touchdowns. If Henry can keep Baltimore out of third-and-long, the Texans' third-most sacks in the NFL matter less -- and QB Jacoby Brissett can get the ball out quickly to WR Zay Flowers.

Brissett is also 5-2 outright against Houston over the course of his career. And with the Texans being one of the most penalized teams in the league, Baltimore could turn those mistakes into extra chances to score.

Indianapolis Colts +6.5 (+260 moneyline) vs. New York Giants

The Giants' defense is struggling to defend the run (4.5 yards allowed per carry), and the Colts can make them defend two runners on the same play. Quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. is making his first start since Week 16 of 2024, while running back Jonathan Taylor should get some help from the threat of Richardson's legs. If Indy can play ball control throughout Sunday's matchup, it can come out on top.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Chop Robinson, Edge, Miami Dolphins: 6 pressures, 1.5 sacks, 23% pass rush win rate

Robinson is, very quietly, leading all edge rushers in pass rush win rate. He hasn't gotten the publicity because that has translated into only five sacks, but playing for the lowly Dolphins (1-9) is a big part of the reason. Teams that are always trailing give their pass rushers far fewer good sack opportunities.

But against the Jets, the Dolphins at least have a chance to get ahead. And Robinson specifically has a shot to get home against Geno Smith, who ranks 27th out of 32 qualifying quarterbacks in sack rate (8.2%). Robinson will face off against a strong right tackle in Armand Membou, which is why the pass rush win rate prediction is a little lower than his standard. However, sack rate is driven by quarterbacks more than anything else.

Jack Bech, WR, Las Vegas Raiders: 5 receptions, 70 yards, 1 touchdown

This is less about buying into Bech's ability after his big game last week -- eight receptions for 88 yards and a score -- and more about buying into anyone who lines up opposite Browns CB Myles Harden. Harden has allowed 1.7 yards per coverage snap this season, per NFL Next Gen Stats, the most of any nickelback with at least 200 coverage snaps. He also shows up poorly in my cornerback player tracking data, which evaluates cornerbacks on their pre-throw positioning.

It's possible the beneficiaries on Sunday night could be one of the Raiders' tight ends, but Harden hasn't frequently matched up against tight ends this season. So Bech, who plays in the slot 42% of the time, might be the one who reaps the rewards.

Bucky Irving, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 22 rushes, 122 rushing yards, 2 touchdowns

Here are some pairs of numbers I'm keeping an eye on: The Buccaneers rank fifth in yards before contact per carry (2.7), while the Panthers' defense ranks 23rd in the same category on defense (2.5). Tampa Bay also ranks third in yards after contact per carry (2.2), while Carolina ranks 29th in the same category on defense (2.9).

Irving, specifically, ranks fourth in both total yards before contact and total yards after contact. I see a big day coming for him Monday night, especially with Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield looking solid in last week's loss to the Lions.

Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders (43.4% rostered in ESPN leagues)

Williams caught nine of a career-high 11 targets and scored 21.2 fantasy points against the Bengals on Monday night. But most importantly, quarterback Jayden Daniels trusted Williams enough to target him twice on the game-winning drive, including a 42-yard completion.

Williams is firmly on the flex radar against a Cardinals defense that has allowed the most passing touchdowns and 12th-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. (He has an even better matchup in Week 13 against the Titans, who are allowing the most fantasy points per game to the position.)

Dylan Sampson, RB, Cleveland Browns (25.1%)

Sampson has played more snaps than running back Quinshon Judkins in three consecutive games -- and Sampson has at least six targets in each of those games. Since returning from injured reserve, he has scored at least 7.7 fantasy points in four consecutive games without scoring a touchdown.

Judkins' presence limits Sampson's upside, but Sampson's involvement in the passing game makes him an intriguing flex option in deeper formats. It also helps that the Raiders' defense has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to running backs.

Deshaun Watson, QB, Cleveland Browns (24.8%)

Watson faces a Raiders defense that has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. He finished with a season-high 21.3 fantasy points against the Texans in Week 10 before Cleveland's bye. Watson has scored at least 21 fantasy points in two of his past three games. The Raiders rank 27th in pass rush win rate, so he should have ample time to find his receivers Sunday.

Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers

Justin Jefferson, WR, Minnesota Vikings

In the two games since the Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins, Jefferson has caught 16 of 22 targets for 160 yards. But he has yet to score a touchdown with Cousins. I'm expecting that to change Sunday against the Falcons. Atlanta is allowing 239.1 passing yards per game (third most in the NFL) and has given up 19 touchdown passes (sixth most).

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Judkins has scored at least one touchdown in two of his past four games, plus he gets consistent volume in the low red zone. He has 12 goal-to-go carries this season, including two or more in four straight games.

Cleveland wants to run the ball on the doorstep of the end zone, and it gets a favorable matchup for that against the Raiders. Las Vegas' defense has allowed 14 rushing scores this season (tied for third most in the NFL).

Mike Evans, WR, San Francisco 49ers

In the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Seahawks, Evans caught seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown. He now has a touchdown grab in two of his past three games played -- he missed three weeks with Achilles tendinitis -- and an end zone target in four of his past five. Quarterback Mac Jones -- who is starting with Brock Purdy out -- is going to look for Evans when the 49ers are in the red zone Sunday.

Solak makes four more predictions

The Texans will blow out the Ravens

While Pamela is predicting an upset, I'm expecting Houston to come out of the gates hot with playoff hopes on the line. What a run for the Texans, who felt like they were out of the AFC playoff picture ... until Patriots QB Drake Maye fractured his fibula and QB Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on the Steelers.

If Houston wins against the Ravens, who are on a six-game skid, and then against the Steelers in Week 13 after this drama-filled week, they'll be .500 and well positioned for the No. 7 seed.

Raiders TE Brock Bowers will have a career day

There is no coach in the world, I think, who loves Bowers like Todd Monken does. The Browns coach was the Georgia Bulldogs' offensive coordinator when Bowers developed into an elite receiving tight end. Now Bowers will get his first real action with quarterback Fernando Mendoza against an old mentor, and Mendoza is throwing the ball well through his first two games.

Bowers' highest-volume game is a 13-catch performance as a rookie. If the weather holds enough that passing is successful, I could see him hitting or exceeding that number.

The Vikings will hold the Falcons scoreless

Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has the second-worst EPA per pressured dropback in the league this season, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Only free agent Daniel Jones is worse. Brian Flores' defense, which just came off its first embarrassing performance of the season, has the league's highest pressure rate by a mile.

You see where I'm going with this. I think Minnesota's defense has a statement performance Sunday as it quickly recovers from the loss to the 49ers.

The Buccaneers will win

After all, the Bucs are favored by three points. But more importantly, if they don't beat the Panthers on Monday night, then Carolina will have a winning record atop the NFC South. That feels spiritually unsound. That division does not deserve a team above .500. Tampa Bay does the right thing and keeps the NFC South grimy with a low-scoring win to stay, technically, in the playoff race.

stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Qatar for the second leg of its final triple header of the 2026 season.

Max Verstappen fended off his rivals to take a stunning victory under the lights at the Las Vegas Grand Prix last time out.

McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took the final spots on the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 22nd round.

- Max Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas

Qatar Grand Prix schedule
All times in GMT

Friday, November 27

Kimi Antonelli quickest in disrupted second practice

Saturday, November 28

Final Practice: 2.30 p.m. - 3.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 6 p.m. - 7 p.m.

Sunday, November 29

Qatar Grand Prix: 4 p.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Qatar Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Lusail Circuit

The Qatar Grand Prix takes place under the floodlights at the Lusail Circuit. It is one of the most demanding on the calendar with long straights and sweeping high-speed corners coupled with intense heat and humidity, making conditions for the cars and drivers difficult.

It was originally built as a motorbike circuit before it joined the F1 calendar in 2021 on a 10-year contract. Qatar did not host a race in 2022 as they focused on the FIFA World Cup.

Qatar Grand Prix

Circuit: Lusail International Circuit; Lusail, Qatar

Previous winners in Qatar

2021: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2023: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2024: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2021

Laps: 57 laps of 5.4km

Lap record: 1:22.384, Lando Norris (2024)

Most wins: Verstappen (2023, 2024 and 2025). Lewis Hamilton (2021) is the only other winner.

Most poles: Hamilton (2021), Verstappen (2023), George Russell (2024) and Piastri (2025) have each taken pole.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Qatar Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny with a gentle breeze across the weekend. It's a night race so conditions are dry with highs of 24°C on Sunday.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Piastri pipped teammate Norris to pole position as the battle for the world title continued with two races remaining.

During the race, Red Bull's Verstappen benefited from a McLaren strategy error to win his seventh race of the season, taking the three-way title race to the season finale in Abu Dhabi.

Piastri was leading the race and Norris was running in third, but the Papaya team decided against pitting under the Safety Car. Piastri ended the race in second, with Norris in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Verstappen looked unstoppable in Las Vegas and will be targeting his fifth win of the season in Qatar.

Mercedes' Russell was well in the mix last time out but will be looking to respond after Verstappen said the Englishman was "so far below his level" as their feud intensified.

Both teams look strong, so the rivalry could well continue in Qatar. Drivers up and down the grid will also be limited to 27 laps on each set of tyres, which will play massively into teams' strategies.

Tensions between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Charles Leclerc continue to heat up after boss Fred Vasseur labelled them "unmanageable."

Don't count out new world champion Kimi Antonelli who is always one to watch after an impressive season.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: What to watch in each of Saturday's 13 games
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
A massive Thanksgiving week bonanza of NHL hockey concludes today. After 14 games on Wednesday, there were 15 on Friday and now 13 on Saturday.

Saturday's lineup includes an interconference showdown between top-tier Stanley Cup contenders, another round of the Battle of Florida, Connor Hellebuyck vs. his former teammates and two Eastern mega-powers squaring off in Carolina.

Read on for a look at what you need to know for each of the games, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Montreal Canadiens at Vegas Golden Knights

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -122, O/U: 6.5

The Saturday slate gets rolling quickly with two of the NHL's final four from the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs ... who both have legitimate cause for thinking they'll get back there again in 2027.

According to Stathletes, there is a 0.56% chance of this being the Stanley Cup Final this season, which would be a superb experience as two of the most magical cities in North America would be center stage.

Montreal made a big trade swing this week with the acquisition of Dylan Larkin from the Red Wings. In theory, this gives Montreal the kind of center depth that is required of a top-tier contender. In practice, the Habs are still looking for their first win with Larkin in the lineup.

Vegas is typically in the mix when any star player is rumored to be on the move, though GM Kelly McCrimmon has not made his statement trade yet this season.

The Golden Knights have statistical edges in goals per game (3.30 to 2.92), goals against per game (2.93 to 3.04), on the power play (27.4% to 13.5%) and penalty kill (80.3% to 78.7%). So who takes Round 1 of this matchup, with Round 2 taking place on Dec. 8 in Montreal?

Tampa Bay Lightning at Florida Panthers

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -105, O/U: 6.5

If the Battle of Florida isn't the top NHL rivalry right now, it's certainly close, as both teams are squarely in a Cup contention window. To wit, from 2020 through 2025, either the Lightning or Panthers appeared in every Stanley Cup Final -- and won four of the six championships.

Tampa sits a point ahead of Florida with one fewer game, as both are in the Atlantic Division logjam. However, the 2026-27 Panthers season can be split into two parts: pre-Aleksander Barkov return and everything after. With the captain back in the mix, the Panthers are a different team.

Nikita Kucherov is a key player to watch for the Lightning. That's true of any game, but he has been particularly inspired against the Panthers with 23 goals and 28 assists in 42 career games vs. Florida.

Nashville Predators at Detroit Red Wings

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -112, O/U: 5.5

The Predators have been quite a pleasant surprise this season, currently battling for one of the Western wild-card spots despite modest expectations heading into the campaign.

On the other side, the Red Wings were a difficult team to predict, given the roster uncertainty; Larkin has now been traded, but Simon Edvinsson's situation remains unresolved. It's not entirely unsurprising that Detroit is among the teams close to the Eastern Conference basement.

Filip Forsberg (nine goals, 17 assists) leads Nashville in scoring heading into this one, while Lucas Raymond (10 goals, 13 assists) tops Detroit's leaderboard.

Winnipeg Jets at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -192, O/U: 6.5

There was considerable angst and no shortage of takes when the Devils announced that Connor Hellebuyck would not be starting when the team visited Winnipeg to take on his former team on Nov. 10.

Perhaps the hockey gods guided the Jets to a 4-2 victory in that contest.

Ask and ye shall receive, as the return matchup on Saturday will include Hellebuyck between the pipes for New Jersey.

The Devils and Jets both come into this matchup having won three straight games. New Jersey is second in the Metro Division, while Winnipeg is fifth in the Central and in possession of the second Western wild card.

On an individual basis, Jack Hughes leads the Devils in scoring (11 goals, 23 assists), while Kyle Connor paces the Jets (22 goals, 16 assists).

Calgary Flames at New York Rangers

7 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | NYR -185, O/U: 5.5

There have not been a ton of memorable games between the Flames and Rangers in history, but the teams had a tightly contested matchup in Calgary on Nov. 11.

The Rangers won that game 3-1, with a pair of Mika Zibanejad goals being enough support for Joonas Korpisalo to earn the W.

The Flames will be looking for some vengeance for that game, and seeking to get back on track after a 5-3 loss to the Devils on Friday in which they led 3-2 after two periods.

Toronto Maple Leafs at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | PIT -122, O/U: 6.5

To put it charitably, there have been Maple Leafs-Penguins games with more on the line in seasons past. Pittsburgh (18 points through 25 games) and Toronto (23 through 27) are both struggling to get on a winning path this season.

Nevertheless, as with any Toronto-Pittsburgh game there are a number of superstars who will be hitting the ice. Auston Matthews has 14 goals and 20 assists through 27 games, on pace for 43 and 62, respectively.

On the other side, Penguins defenseman Erik Karlsson has 21 points through 25 games -- which is on pace for 70 for the season ... a season which he may finish playing for a different team, if the trade speculation is to be believed.

Ottawa Senators at Carolina Hurricanes

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -238, O/U: 6.5

Game of the night? The current leaders of the Atlantic and Metro Divisions met in the first round of the 2026 playoffs -- a series that started with a fight between captains Jordan Staal and Brady Tkachuk, and ended with a Hurricanes sweep.

Tkachuk is gone, but the rest of that Senators core remains, and they'll be looking to set the tone in the first of three matchups between the clubs this regular season.

One other fun factor here: Germany's Tim Stutzle (15 goals, 18 assists) and Finland's Sebastian Aho (13 goals, 21 assists) are the Senators' and Hurricanes' leading scorers, respectively, bringing some international flavor to the mix.

Washington Capitals at St. Louis Blues

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | STL -112, O/U: 6.5

Ah, what could've been. In theory, this would have been the first game back in St. Louis for Jordan Kyrou, who was traded to the Capitals this summer. Unfortunately, he's on injured reserve with an upper-body injury (after posting 14 points in 21 games).

The Caps will see a familiar face on the opposite side of the ice in this one, as Connor McMichael was part of the package that went to St. Louis for Kyrou. McMichael has 11 points through 23 games.

Zoomed out a bit, this game also pits two teams that need every point they can get from here on out. The Capitals begin the day nine points back of the final Eastern wild-card spot, and seven back of No. 3 in the Metro. The Blues are one point back of the final wild-card spot in the West, and one back of third place in the Central (it's a very tight division).

New York Islanders at Philadelphia Flyers

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -118, O/U: 6.5

Given that these two are in the same division, there should be a bit more rivalry juice. But, they've met just five times in the playoffs, with the 2020 second round being the most recent (a 4-3 series win by the Isles).

As far as this season goes, the Flyers have shown more gusto recently, including back-to-back wins over the Senators and Canadiens (before getting blown out by the Capitals).

The Isles have been steadily adding points in the standings. As play begins Saturday, the Isles are third in the Metro, while the Flyers are fifth.

From an individual standpoint, Matthew Schaefer is the player to watch for New York; his 26 points (nine goals, 17 assists) lead the team. Philly is led by Matvei Michkov (11 goals, nine assists), though he was scratched from Friday's game for an "internal team matter."

It's never boring with the Flyers, is it?

Utah Mammoth at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -162, O/U: 5.5

As alluded above, there is an absolute logjam in the Central Division right now, with just two points separating No. 2 from No. 7. Both of these teams are in that band of teams, so games like this one take on added meaning -- particularly since their remaining three games this season are in March and April.

Both teams played the Predators within the past week, though the game style was quite different in each case: the Mammoth won 6-5 in a shootout, while the Stars lost 3-1 in regulation.

Given those results, it's not surprising to see that the Mammoth are well ahead of the Stars in goal scoring (3.37 per game vs. 2.68), but also well behind in goal suppression (allowing 3.38 to the Stars' 2.48). Will this one be a high-flying scorefest, or a defensive battle?

San Jose Sharks at Colorado Avalanche

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -278, O/U: 6.5

As the Sharks continue their push to be among the playoff contenders, games like this one -- against an actual playoff contender -- are a vital barometer.

It's the first of three matchups this season between the two clubs, and this will likely be San Jose's only chance of the season to get a win off of Colorado without Nathan MacKinnon in the lineup. The All-World center is out until mid-February with a lower-body injury.

However, the Avs' other super-duper-star, Cale Makar, made his return to the lineup on Wednesday, finishing with three assists in Colorado's 6-0 win over Montreal, then scoring the game-winning goal in the shootout against Minnesota on Friday.

For what it's worth, Sharks leading scorer Macklin Celebrini has not been particularly great against the Avs to this point of his career, with just two points in five games.

Anaheim Ducks at Los Angeles Kings

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -142, O/U: 6.5

Wait, didn't these two teams just play on Friday? They sure did, a 5-3 win for the Kings in Anaheim.

It was a game of scoring streaks, as Stian Solberg notched two in the first for Anaheim before Mats Zuccarello scored two for L.A. in the second. Adrian Kempe put the Kings ahead, but was quickly matched by Beckett Sennecke. Andre Lee scored the go-ahead goal 2:16 into the third, and Trevor Moore added an empty-netter.

Have the Ducks been grounded? The loss on Friday gives them five regulation defeats in their last six games. On the other side, the Kings have won four of their last five after a four-game losing streak near the start of the month.

Can Anaheim get revenge on Saturday and start to get back on track? Or does SoCal belong to the Kings again?

Edmonton Oilers at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -170, O/U: 6.5

Just like the Ducks and Kings, these two teams also just played on Friday. That game was in Edmonton, while this one will be in Seattle.

The Friday game ended 4-2 in favor of the Kraken. Both Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl scored goals for the Oilers, but apparently that isn't enough when Kaapo Kakko is on the other roster! The Finn scored the game-tying and go-ahead goals in quick succession in the third period, before Vince Dunn sealed the deal with an empty-netter.

Following the win, the Kraken are now just one point back of the Sharks for third place in the Pacific, with five games in hand. Meanwhile, the Oilers remain on top of the division, with a three-point edge over the Golden Knights. How will things look after Saturday?

stories.headline: Lakers' Luka Doncic has altercation with fan after NBA Cup loss to Spurs
stories.summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic was shoved by a fan following Friday's loss to the Spurs in a brief altercation that he chalked up as a postgame ritual gone awry.
stories.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic had a brief altercation with a fan in the aftermath of Friday night's 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center.

Doncic, 27, chalked up the situation as a postgame ritual gone awry.

"I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game," Doncic said. "Then, I heard he didn't want it, so I went back to grab it. He just pushed me. Then, I gave it to somebody else."

The altercation took place as Doncic walked off the floor and headed toward the visitors' locker room just minutes after the Lakers were eliminated from the NBA Cup, becoming the first team this season to squander multiple 20-point leads.

Video from Amazon Prime's postgame broadcast showed Doncic walking past a man and a woman sitting courtside and throwing a white wristband in their direction.

The woman appeared to say something to Doncic just before he tossed the wristband. But just as quickly, Doncic turned around to retrieve it. The man next to the woman picked the wristband up and handed it to Doncic before shoving him as he turned to walk back toward the locker room.

The shove jolted Doncic somewhat and teammate Jarred Vanderbilt stepped in to intervene along with members of Frost Bank Center security. The man was subsequently ejected.

"I just heard somebody say they didn't want it," Doncic said. "I went back to get it, and then he pushed me. I just gave the wristband to somebody else."

It's unclear whether Doncic will face any discipline from the NBA.

Los Angeles led Friday's contest by 20 points in the second quarter and by 16 at intermission before San Antonio outscored the Lakers 30-14 in the third quarter. Reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year Keldon Johnson tied the score at 68 with 1.8 seconds left in the frame with a 23-foot corner 3-pointer. The Spurs got a combined 17 points from Stephon Castle (nine points) and Victor Wembanyama (eight points) in the fourth quarter to pull out the win.

Doncic scored a game-high 31 points on 31 attempts for his 12th 30-point game of the season, tying two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander for the most in the NBA.

"The reality is, that's the barometer in the West right now, and this was a great test for us," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "We'll get better from it. They're disappointed right now and it's a natural emotion from losing a game. I told them this morning, 'We're going to get feedback [from the game]. And when we wake up tomorrow, if we've won the game or lost, we're still a good team on Saturday morning.'"

ESPN Research contributed to this report.
